scope: Standalone fixture safety helper and bounded ordinary-user unit CI; not an integrated or privileged runtime result.
behavior: Fixed bootstrap source is intended for independent administrator authorization. It opens bounded held regular-file bytes and authenticates the exact digest before compiling and executing the accepted immutable bytes.
Descriptor-relative metadata acquisition rejects links and special files before the read-open, then checks the opened inode and enforces file and aggregate byte bounds.
The collector accepts only LIVE.json, DONE.json and result.json under the declared reduced credentials, and retains missing/refused outcomes.

validation.linux_native_test: SKIPPED on Windows; not counted as passed
independent_additional_checks: Wrong reopened inode refused before any read and descriptors closed
Authenticated SystemExit propagated with original argv restored
validation.static: Generated bootstrap closes over standard-library imports; pyflakes reported zero findings
validation.reviews: Two independent Sols approved the exact final helper, tests and bounded non-root CI addition with zero unresolved objections in that scope.
validation.ci: One 45-second command with a two-second kill grace added to the existing Ubuntu minimum-toolchain job, under a two-minute step bound. Native execution is pending at this publication.

limits: The existing privileged packet has not been integrated or executed. Current root entry, ordinary evidence acquisition and unsafe service teardown remain withheld.

The launcher must independently authorize the exact generated bootstrap and arguments, establish trusted procfs and ancestor custody, clear capabilities and inherited authority, and enforce a native whole-process deadline.
Matching stat metadata does not prove an atomic snapshot of mutable ordinary records; those records remain untrusted. A supplied fixed digest authenticates the accepted fixture-code bytes.
Full-lifetime exclusive activation and verified safe teardown of stock services remain required. This helper does not establish VM lifetime or isolation.
The guard's Rust source and six stock Linux product/deployment assets are unchanged. No speed, parity, backend qualification or issue-closure claim follows.
